name: Entecavir
drug_class: Nucleoside analogue HBV polymerase inhibitor (carbocyclic guanosine analogue)
route_note: oral tablet or solution once daily on an empty stomach

discovery.note: Carbocyclic deoxyguanosine analogue originally investigated against herpesviruses, found to be highly potent against HBV.

tagline: Potent, high-barrier first-line oral drug for chronic hepatitis B
summary: Entecavir is a guanosine nucleoside analogue that strongly suppresses hepatitis B virus replication. Together with tenofovir it is a first-line treatment for chronic hepatitis B, with a very low rate of resistance in previously untreated patients. Long-term use reduces liver inflammation and fibrosis and lowers the risk of cirrhosis complications.
mechanism: Entecavir is phosphorylated in cells to entecavir triphosphate, which competes with deoxyguanosine triphosphate and inhibits all three activities of the HBV polymerase: priming, reverse transcription of pregenomic RNA and synthesis of positive-strand DNA.

Resistance in treatment-naive patients is rare (about 1% after 5 years), but prior lamivudine resistance (rtM204V/I) lowers the barrier. Entecavir has weak anti-HIV activity and can select the M184V mutation in untreated HIV.
uses: Chronic hepatitis B in adults and children aged 2 years and older with active viral replication and liver inflammation
Chronic hepatitis B with decompensated liver disease

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Baraclude is approved in March 2005; EU approval follows in 2006.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Baraclude is approved in the EU in June 2006.

history.title: HIV warning
history.detail: Reports that entecavir can select M184V in HIV co-infection lead to recommendations against use without effective HIV therapy.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic entecavir becomes available in the US.

history.title: WHO guidelines
history.detail: WHO's first hepatitis B guidelines recommend entecavir or tenofovir as first-line therapy.

pk.half_life: terminal about 128–149 h; intracellular triphosphate about 15 h
pk.bioavailability: at least 70%; taken on an empty stomach
pk.metabolism: not a CYP substrate; minor glucuronidation

serious: severe acute exacerbation of hepatitis B on discontinuation
lactic acidosis and hepatomegaly, particularly in decompensated disease
selection of HIV resistance in untreated co-infection
safety.boxed_warning: Severe acute exacerbations of hepatitis B on discontinuation; HIV/HBV co-infection (risk of HIV resistance); lactic acidosis and hepatomegaly (US label).

facts: Entecavir is one of the most potent anti-HBV drugs, with a daily dose of only 0.5–1 mg.
In China, where generic entecavir is inexpensive, it is one of the most widely used hepatitis B treatments.
